items.title: 2026-2027 DWU: Middle School Design Challenge
items.summary: The “Fueling Flight Design Challenge: New Energy Systems” asks student teams to redesign an airport so it can handle both traditional aviation fuel and liquefied natural gas. Submissions are open to grades 6–8 through January 22, 2027.

items.title: 2026-2027 DWU: High School Engineering Challenge
items.summary: The high school module of NASA’s Dream with Us challenge opens September 25, 2026, with teams designing the aircraft, airport infrastructure, and safety case for a new liquid natural gas fuel system.

items.title: NASA, Northrop Grumman Complete Cygnus XL Space Station Reboost
items.summary: Northrop Grumman’s Cygnus XL spacecraft fired its thrusters for 18 minutes, raising the International Space Station’s orbit by about 1.5 miles at apogee. The reboost sets up phasing for NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission.

items.title: The Scale of the Universe – Great Debate in 1996
items.summary: Six published papers from the 1996 debate over the value of the Hubble constant, the number that sets the scale and age of our universe. A reminder that cosmology advances through argument as much as observation.

items.title: Globular Cluster Omega Centauri
items.summary: Omega Centauri packs about 10 million stars much older than the Sun into a volume some 150 light-years across. Two decades of Hubble observations found evidence for a massive black hole near its center.

items.title: Explosive Intensification for Hurricane Polo
items.summary: NASA’s Earth Observatory tracked Hurricane Polo as it rapidly intensified, using satellite observations to follow the storm’s structure and strength from orbit.

items.title: NASA to Study Human Health, Performance During Crew-13 Mission
items.summary: Experiments flying with NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission will measure how the human body adapts to microgravity, from cardiovascular changes to immune response, ahead of longer flights to the Moon and Mars.

items.title: US-India Satellite Captures Time-lapse Video of Volcanic Eruption
items.summary: NISAR, the joint NASA-ISRO radar satellite, recorded a volcanic eruption in time-lapse, showing how the ground itself deformed as magma moved beneath the surface.

items.title: Visual Distortions Near a Black Hole and Neutron Star
items.summary: A NASA visualization of how extreme gravity bends light itself, warping the view of the sky around a black hole and its neutron star companion.

items.title: The Ghosts of Five Supernovas
items.summary: About 200 hours of observations from Morocco reveal five supernova remnants in Auriga, their expanding shells of shocked gas glowing in hydrogen red and oxygen blue.

items.title: A New Lunar Crater: McGetchin
items.summary: NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter caught a fresh crater roughly two soccer fields wide that formed between April and May 2024 — an impact expected only once every 132 years.

items.title: Cloudy Cloak Over the Northwest
items.summary: A satellite view of marine fog and cloud banks settling over the Pacific Northwest, part of NASA’s daily look at how weather shapes the view from above.

items.title: NASA-Funded Research Finds Complex Life Defying Record Heat
items.summary: NASA-supported scientists discovered an organism living at temperatures previously thought impossible for complex life, widening the range of environments where life might survive elsewhere.

items.title: Risks of Decompression Sickness and Venous Thromboembolism during Spaceflight
items.summary: NASA’s Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer summarizes current evidence on decompression sickness and blood-clot risk in spaceflight, and what a patent foramen ovale may mean for astronauts.

items.title: NASA Astronaut to Answer Questions from New Hampshire Students
items.summary: Students in New Hampshire got a live downlink with an astronaut aboard the International Space Station, asking about life and research in orbit.

items.title: Chance Triple Alignment: Plane, Space Station, Sun
items.summary: A split-second exposure from the Czech Republic caught the International Space Station and an airplane crossing the Sun at the same time — a roughly 30-million-to-one coincidence.

items.title: NASA Discovery Reveals Complex Water Systems on Early Mars
items.summary: Mastcam-Z images from the Perseverance rover’s Turquoise Bay panorama add detail to the story of water on early Mars, outlining a landscape shaped by more than one kind of watery environment.

items.title: Cocoon Nebula Wide Field
items.summary: IC 5146, the Cocoon Nebula, sits at the head of a nearly 100-light-year trail of dust in Cygnus. The dark filaments hide stars still in the process of forming.

items.title: Embracing the Equinox
items.summary: The September equinox marks the moment day and night are nearly equal around the world — a good excuse to look up, and a reminder of Earth’s tilt in space.

items.title: Analemma over the Callanish Stones
items.summary: Images taken at noon for a year from the Outer Hebrides trace the Sun’s figure-eight path, shaped by Earth’s axial tilt and its elliptical orbit.

items.title: A Zodiacal Night
items.summary: Zodiacal light — sunlight scattered by interplanetary dust — glows before dawn over the Hanle Dark Sky Reserve in Ladakh, India, with Jupiter and Mars caught in the band.

items.title: Messier 33: The Triangulum Galaxy
items.summary: M33 is over 50,000 light-years across and about 3 million light-years away — third largest in our Local Group and a cosmic yardstick for measuring the scale of the universe.

items.title: NASA’s Hubble Spots an Out-of-Sync Galaxy
items.summary: Hubble imagery highlights a galaxy whose stars and gas are oddly out of step with one another, the kind of mismatch that hints at a disturbed past.

items.title: NASA’s Moon Orbiter Spots New, ‘Once-in-Century’ Moon Crater
items.summary: The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter’s monthly monitoring revealed a crater about 728 feet wide that appeared on the Moon in 2024, the largest freshly formed crater ever identified.

items.title: NASA-JAXA XRISM Mission Sees Pulsar Gathering Companion’s ‘Wind’
items.summary: XRISM watched a pulsar sweep up material from the stellar wind of its companion star, a laboratory for understanding how matter behaves under extreme gravity.

items.title: Helio and You: A Fresh Perspective on the Sun
items.summary: A guided look at how NASA studies the Sun’s atmosphere and magnetic field, and why solar activity matters all the way down here on Earth.

items.title: A Treasure Chest in the Carina Nebula
items.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope peered into a dust pillar in the Carina Nebula, finding a cluster of about 70 young stars — including one roughly 19 times the mass of the Sun.
